name: _sparse_softmax
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::_sparse_softmax(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float) -> Tensor. Not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, mutation and aliasing contract, and tests must never be narrowed or the reference adapted to fit this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::_sparse_softmax.Dimname(Tensor self, str dim, *, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor; aten::_sparse_softmax.int(Tensor self, int dim, ScalarType? dtype=None) -> Tensor; aten::_sparse_softmax.out(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!); aten::_sparse_softmax(Tensor self, int dim, bool half_to_float) -> Tensor. Semantics derived from the tests: softmax normalization along the requested dim of a sparse COO tensor, including hybrid COO tensors whose trailing axes are dense value blocks; for hybrid inputs dim may also index a dense value axis, including the fully dense sparse_dim 0 form. The tests compare the candidate result, including its is_coalesced() flag, against the reference result rather than asserting that the output is coalesced. The candidate public entry point is flag_gems._sparse_softmax called with the same arguments. Schema-dependent behavior that this single-overload model does not express conditionally: this representative .default form takes a required positional half_to_float with no default, whereas the .int overload takes an optional ScalarType dtype defaulting to null (the pytest also exercises the omitted-dtype call, which keeps the input dtype) and, on the NVIDIA target where those kernel limits were measured and gated by device capability flags, covers dtype= conversion of int8/uint8/int32/int64/bfloat16/fp8 inputs to float32/float64; the .Dimname overload accepts a str dim; the .out overload takes a required keyword-only out buffer and declares the return as aliasing it, and the pytest asserts that the candidate both writes that buffer and returns the same buffer object. Kind, requiredness and null defaults come from the supplied schema metadata; no non-JSON ATen defaults occur here, since the only optional argument (dtype) is JSON null in the overloads that have it.
